title: Complicated intra-abdominal infection on piperacillin-tazobactam plus metronidazole

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), case list approved by the owner

clinical_review.notes: Owner clinical review: cases look good.

story: A 41-year-old man has a laparoscopic appendectomy for perforated appendicitis with localized peritonitis. He is started on piperacillin-tazobactam and metronidazole. Source control is adequate and he is improving on postoperative day 1.

results.text: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

expected_findings.summary: Piperacillin-tazobactam already covers anaerobes; adding metronidazole duplicates anaerobic coverage.

reference_answer: Stop metronidazole and continue piperacillin-tazobactam alone; with adequate source control, plan a short total course of about 4 days.
rationale: Piperacillin-tazobactam has reliable activity against Bacteroides and other intra-abdominal anaerobes. Adding metronidazole adds toxicity and cost without clinical benefit. Duration is not the case's finding, but the reference answer notes it.

citations.supports: Single-agent regimens with anaerobic activity, including piperacillin-tazobactam, for complicated intra-abdominal infection; about 4 days after adequate source control.
Prospective audit and feedback of antibiotic therapy as a stewardship intervention.
